summary: Sum the GSEQ imethod==1 closed-form filament-coil Green responses (poloidal flux psi = R A_phi, radial field B_r, axial field B_z) over ring coils, consuming caller-supplied per-coil elliptic values and the source-regularized observation radius.

identity.relation: relation_variant_of: scirel.field.circular-filament-green (same circular-filament Green physics, different evaluation contract). Per coil: flux_l = factor/sqrt(m)*sqrt(r0*rl)*((2-m)K - 2E); br_l = factor*dz/r0/distance*((r0^2+rl^2+dz^2)/sep^2*E - K); bz_l = factor/distance*((rl^2-r0^2-dz^2)/sep^2*E + K); summed linearly with factor = 2e-7*turns*current.
identity.direction: regularized observation point + per-coil geometry/current/turns + per-coil squared moduli and K, E values -> total flux, B_r, B_z responses (scalars)
identity.definition: The GSEQ imethod==1 closed-form coil response (fun_Bfield.m:10-27). The relation is the same circular-filament Green physics as the baseline scirel.field.circular-filament-green; this variant's contract differences are: (i) K, E are caller-supplied per coil (typically the GSEQ apx==1 approximation for provenance parity) instead of internally evaluated scipy special functions; (ii) one scalar observation point per call with the source's r0 + 1e-8 axis regularization applied once upstream (not inside this operator); (iii) current and turns enter through the combined 2e-7*N*I factor; (iv) singular geometries are rejected fail-closed instead of the baseline's zeroing of non-finite terms.
identity.model: original GSEQ MATLAB imethod==1 closed-form arrangement with registered singular-geometry and nonfinite-output rejections
identity.geometry: one scalar observation point; ncoil ring coils; per-coil closed-form responses summed linearly
identity.coordinates: cylindrical R-Z, SI metres; flux in Wb/rad (psi = R A_phi convention, not the 2*pi ring-flux), fields in tesla
identity.boundary: finite aligned inputs; strictly positive regularized radius and coil radii; moduli in (0, 1) after singular rejection; observation point on a filament ring (zero separation, modulus == 1) is rejected instead of returning the source's NaN responses
assumptions: Moduli and K, E pairings arrive per coil by index, typically from the coil Green geometry and complete-elliptic-integrals operators.
The flux convention is psi = R A_phi (Wb/rad), shared with the baseline filament Green relations; it is not the full 2*pi ring flux.
No external physics reference is bound beyond the shared circular-filament closed form.

inputs.name: regularized_radius_m
inputs.description: Observation radius after the source axis offset (from the coil Green geometry operator).
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; the offset is applied once upstream and is not repeated here.

inputs.name: coil_radius_m
inputs.constraints: Finite 1-D, strictly positive entries, shared shape with the other coil vectors.

inputs.name: modulus_squared
inputs.description: Per-coil squared elliptic modulus m = k^2.
inputs.constraints: Finite; entries in (0, 1) after singular rejection; exactly 1 marks an observation point on a filament ring and is rejected.

inputs.name: complete_k
inputs.description: Per-coil first-kind complete elliptic integral K(m).
inputs.constraints: Finite where modulus != 1 (the singular-geometry rejection makes non-finite pairings unreachable on accepted inputs).

inputs.name: complete_e
inputs.description: Per-coil second-kind complete elliptic integral E(m).

outputs.name: flux_weber
outputs.description: Total poloidal-flux response psi = R A_phi summed over coils.
outputs.units: Wb/rad (per the psi = R A_phi convention; subject to the caller's current units)
outputs.constraints: Finite on accepted inputs; overflow from finite but extreme currents/turns raises ValueError (registered hardening).

outputs.name: radial_field_t
outputs.description: Total radial field response B_r summed over coils.
outputs.constraints: Finite on accepted inputs; overflow from finite but extreme currents/turns raises ValueError (registered hardening).

outputs.name: axial_field_t
outputs.description: Total axial field response B_z summed over coils.
outputs.constraints: Finite on accepted inputs; overflow from finite but extreme currents/turns raises ValueError (registered hardening).

preconditions: Per-coil geometry, currents, turns and elliptic pairings exist with aligned shapes (typically from the coil Green geometry and complete-elliptic-integrals operators).
The observation radius carries the source axis offset exactly once.
supported: GSEQ filament-coil Green response summation with caller-supplied elliptic values for provenance-parity chains.
excluded: Arbitrary-point (array-target) Green evaluation, internal special-function evaluation (that is the baseline circular-filament relation), modulus generation, coil geometry construction, and ideal-conductor boundary corrections.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when the observation coordinates are non-finite or the radius non-positive, when coil vectors are misaligned or contain non-positive radii or non-finite values, when moduli lie outside (0, 1), when elliptic pairings are non-finite on non-singular geometry, or when the observation point coincides with a filament ring (zero separation, modulus == 1; registered singular-geometry rejection). The inputs are additionally checked for overflow-level magnitudes at the output stage (registered hardening).
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if any response overflows to a non-finite value for finite but extreme input magnitudes (registered hardening); no partial results are returned.

provenance.lineage_summary: Development integration from the saved GSEQ filament-coil Green package and original MATLAB imethod==1 source anchor. SciRel preserves the accepted-input closed-form arrangement but adds explicit singular-geometry and nonfinite-output rejection; the saved Python package may return nonfinite values on those boundaries. Source comparison and cross-implementation tests support bounded development review, not qualified D1 provenance, expert approval or public release.

python.signature: evaluate_filament_coil_green_field(regularized_radius_m, observation_z_m, coil_radius_m, coil_z_m, current_a, turns, modulus_squared, complete_k, complete_e)

example.description: Evaluate the Green response of a mirrored coil pair on the midplane; the radial components cancel and the response scales linearly with current.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import (
    compute_axisymmetric_coil_modulus,
    evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals,
    evaluate_filament_coil_green_field,
)
radius, modulus, _ = compute_axisymmetric_coil_modulus(
    0.3, 0.0, np.array([0.2, 0.2]), np.array([-0.1, 0.1]))
k, e = evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals(modulus)
flux, br, bz = evaluate_filament_coil_green_field(
    radius, 0.0, np.array([0.2, 0.2]), np.array([-0.1, 0.1]),
    np.array([10.0, 10.0]), np.array([2.0, 2.0]), modulus, k, e)
assert abs(br) < 1e-18
flux2, br2, bz2 = evaluate_filament_coil_green_field(
    radius, 0.0, np.array([0.2, 0.2]), np.array([-0.1, 0.1]),
    np.array([20.0, 20.0]), np.array([2.0, 2.0]), modulus, k, e)
assert flux2 == 2.0 * flux and bz2 == 2.0 * bz
example.expected: The mirrored pair cancels B_r on the midplane; doubling the currents doubles every response; an observation point on a coil ring raises ValueError instead of returning NaN.

scope: Closed-form responses against an independent recomputation.
Cross-implementation agreement with the baseline scipy-elliptic filament relation at equal elliptic values.
Singular-geometry rejection and input failure contracts.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The maintained direct tests establish the three responses against an independent closed-form recomputation (exact float equality), linear superposition in current, midplane B_r cancellation of a mirrored pair, and the fail-closed input contracts including the registered singular-geometry rejection. Cross-implementation evidence: with identical scipy-evaluated K, E the GSEQ closed form agrees with the baseline scirel.field.circular-filament-green response to rtol 1e-12 on probed geometries (same physics, different arrangement); feeding the source's polynomial-log approximation instead shifts responses by up to ~1e-5 relative on the probed set, consistent with the approximation's documented ~1e-8 K/E error amplified by the closed form -- sampled evidence over probed geometries, not a continuous bound. No test establishes the responses against an external physics reference beyond the shared closed form.
known_limitations: The saved GSEQ bundle supports bounded historical development comparison only; qualified-L1 delivery root is empty.

This asset is a declared relation variant of scirel.field.circular-filament-green, not a new Green capability; the variant boundary (caller-supplied elliptic values, scalar target, source regularization, fail-closed singulars) must not be collapsed by silent unification.

Registered input hardening chain (documented for the family): the geometry operator rejects raw negative observation radii, and this operator rejects zero-separation/modulus-1 singular geometry; both boundaries are silently accepted (or NaN-returned) by the saved implementations.

Registered output hardening: finite but extreme current/turns magnitudes that overflow the combined response factor raise ValueError instead of returning Inf/NaN (the saved implementation returns them silently).
The singular-geometry rejection (observation point on a filament ring) deliberately diverges from the saved implementation, which returns NaN responses silently on that boundary.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.
